name: Hereditary Sensory and Autonomic Neuropathy Type 4
aliases: Congenital Insensitivity to Pain with Anhidrosis (CIPA)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for HSAN Type IV

criteria.description: Congenital insensitivity to pain and temperature
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the NTRK1 gene
Absent or severely reduced sweat response on quantitative sudomotor axon reflex testing
Nerve biopsy showing loss of small myelinated and unmyelinated fibers

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital insensitivity to pain and anhidrosis with confirmed NTRK1 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Clinical diagnosis is supported by genetic testing and neurophysiological studies.

pathognomonic.notes: Complete inability to perceive nociceptive stimuli from birth
Leads to recurrent episodes of unexplained hyperthermia
Due to impaired thermoregulation from anhidrosis

common.symptomName: Self-mutilating behavior (biting of tongue, lips, fingers)
common.notes: Due to lack of pain perception
Mild to moderate intellectual disability reported
Due to repeated trauma and joint destruction
Often unnoticed due to pain insensitivity

occasional.notes: Due to decreased corneal sensation and injury
Mild muscle tone reduction in some patients
Secondary to skin breakdown and unnoticed injuries
Due to repeated trauma and autonomic dysfunction

laboratory: Absent or reduced sweat response on quantitative sudomotor axon reflex test
imaging: X-rays showing Charcot joints and bone fractures
MRI may show peripheral nerve abnormalities
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in NTRK1 gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
other: Nerve biopsy showing loss of small myelinated and unmyelinated fibers
Absent intraepidermal nerve fibers on skin biopsy

distinguishingFeatures: Multisystem involvement including renal and cardiac

redFlags: Early onset anhidrosis with failure to thrive
references: Indo Y. NTRK1 mutations in congenital insensitivity to pain with anhidrosis. Clin Genet. 2001.
Dyck PJ et al. Hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathies: clinical features and classification. Brain. 1993.
Orphanet: Hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type IV.
